definitions.explanation: Tension or conflict in relationships between people, groups, or nations. Implies ongoing difficulty rather than a single dispute.

examples.japanese: ⟦{両国|りょうこく}→両国：10010_ryoukoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{軋轢|あつれき}
⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{違|ちが}い→違い：03432_chigai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{軋轢|あつれき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|しょう}じた→生じる：02118_shoujiru⟧。
examples.english: Friction arose from differences of opinion.

examples.japanese: ⟦{経営陣|けいえいじん}→経営陣：20535_keieijin⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{労働組合|ろうどうくみあい}→労働組合：16096_roudoukumiai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{間|あいだ}→間：00914_aida⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{軋轢|あつれき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧らしい。
examples.english: There seems to be friction between management and the labor union.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: Originally refers to the creaking/grinding sound of wheels (⟦{軋|きし}む→軋む：07413_kishimu⟧ = to creak, {轢|れき} = wheel). The metaphor extends to interpersonal friction.

FORMALITY: Somewhat formal. Common in news and written language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {軋轢|あつれき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|しょう}じる→生じる：02118_shoujiru⟧/⟦{起|お}きる→起きる：00521_okiru⟧ (friction arises)
- {軋轢|あつれき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{生|う}む→生む：29531_umu⟧ (to create friction)
- {軋轢|あつれき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{避|さ}ける→避ける：02109_sakeru⟧ (to avoid friction)
- ～⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{軋轢|あつれき} (friction with ~)
